feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the positioning is clear, the career progression is logical, and the experience shows real scope across strategy, platforms, analytics, and multimedia. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few style/grammar fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the header summary aligns well with the roles and shows a coherent niche in digital strategy, advocacy communications, and platform modernization.  
- Strong credibility and progression: long tenure at NACo with advancement across multiple roles signals trust, growth, and increasing responsibility.  
- Good use of scale indicators: examples like “10,000+ page website,” “3.5 million annual page views,” and named tools/platforms add substance and specificity.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond scope: include results such as engagement growth, email performance, efficiency gains, cost savings, adoption rates, or campaign impact.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Soft Skills” overlap heavily; consolidate to tighten structure and save space.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: add “of” in “more than 12 years of experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); “French (A2/Learning)” reads awkwardly—use “French (A2, learning)” or “Elementary.”
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, tighter phrasing, and a few specifics that better reflect the most recent roles.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” and lead with current positioning: “Digital communications and strategy leader…”
- Replace broad lists with higher-value themes tied to recent work: enterprise web/CMS modernization, cross-channel governance, analytics, and mission-driven advocacy communications.
- Add a clearer seniority signal such as “leading digital teams and platforms” or “driving organization-wide communications systems.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years’ experience leading web, email, social, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, enterprise web and CMS modernization, and the workflows, governance, and analytics systems that support complex organizations. Strong background in advocacy messaging, stakeholder coordination, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and workflow/systems language overlap with Core Competencies; keep the intro high-level and let skills sections carry the detail.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership areas will make it more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and sharpen wording: “Multi-channel communications,” “Web platform administration,” “Editorial systems design,” “Analytics, reporting & optimization.”
- Prioritize strategic/leadership competencies over execution-heavy items; consider: “Digital strategy & platform modernization • Editorial governance & workflow design • Cross-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS administration • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia production & live events.”
- Replace “Workflow & systems architecture” with “Editorial governance & workflow design” or “Content operations & systems design” for clearer relevance to your recent roles.
- Keep style consistent: use either “and” or “&” throughout, and pluralize “communication” to “communications.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” overlaps with Soft Skills and the header.
- “Multimedia & live event production” is already covered in Topline Skills and multiple experience bullets.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and project footer. Tighten it around 3–4 highest-impact contributions and add outcomes or scale.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client context: “Embedded full-time as strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements across web, campaigns, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery.”
- Consolidate execution bullets: combine “digital systems, workflows and analytics” with governance/operational best practices into one bullet focused on enterprise communications infrastructure.
- Make Drupal/campaign work outcome-led: mention number of microsites/toolkits launched, audience served, or efficiency gains if available.
- Rephrase technical bullet to show business value: “Delivered Drupal CMS enhancements, front-end builds, and troubleshooting for high-traffic public-facing sites” and quantify traffic/size if possible.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep a shorter mention here and let the project section carry detail.
- Governance, analytics, and enterprise web improvement closely repeat the header/Core Competencies; avoid restating all three separately.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management details already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Recast bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make impact more explicit where possible: add results for analytics/governance/video studio (e.g., reporting speed, production cost savings, turnaround time, stakeholder adoption, campaign output).
- Trim generic phrasing like “core digital communications channels” and replace with specifics only if differentiated by scale, growth, or performance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Email/social/video channel management overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, platform modernization, analytics, and governance.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer projects; mention the capability built here, not recurring series execution.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused and emphasize what was built or scaled before promotion.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to stress ownership and scope: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more active and foundational: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing with operational impact: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Improved digital publishing workflows” overlaps with the Director role’s governance/publishing standards; keep this entry focused on execution and team coordination.
- Weekly video updates also appear in the 2015–2018 role; frame this version as scaling/formalizing the series, not originating it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior, recent strengths and use sharper phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with more distinctive, leadership-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy for public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance, publishing standards, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Audience-centered content planning for advocacy and member engagement
- Consider swapping “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “Digital governance and operating models” if you want to stress systems leadership over messaging.
- Keep each line noun-based and specific; avoid broad labels like “leadership” unless paired with scope or channel detail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one version only.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and current strengths rather than listing every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Drop or de-emphasize older/lower-signal items like jQuery unless it is required for target roles.
- Prioritize recent, proven strengths from current/NACo work: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, integrations, workflow systems.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “Enterprise CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” or “AI-enabled search and structured content workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages” duplicates the Technical + IT section; keep Topline Skills broader and more strategic.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies; avoid repeating identical phrasing.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic value and decision-making, not repeat software names alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to capability-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting.”
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity” instead of listing each separately.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger business language like “Executive dashboards and decision support.”
- Consider revised line: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive dashboards and decision support • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI & Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX and performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills more strategic and let Technical + IT hold the full tool list.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader analytics language; “SEO, UX and performance optimization” is cleaner and more distinct.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Make it more senior and outcomes-oriented, emphasizing operational leadership over tool-level detail.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to something broader and more strategic, e.g. “Multimedia Operations & Event Production.”
- Replace the list with tighter, leadership-focused phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • Studio buildout and operations • PTZ and multi-camera production workflows • Virtual event support”
- If space allows, add one impact cue tied to recent work: “Built and operated an in-house studio supporting advocacy programming and recurring event production.”
- Keep only the most distinctive capabilities here; move software/tool specifics to Technical + IT.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- “Studio operations” and “Livestream studio workflows” are also echoed in Technical + IT, so this section should stay higher-level.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills almost exactly. This version should be tighter and, if possible, signal depth in the most recent/important platforms rather than just listing names.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent platforms: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider emphasizing level: “Drupal (enterprise, migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add brief qualifiers instead of a pure list: “Drupal (10,000+ page migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If no qualifiers are possible, shorten the heading to “CMS Platforms” for cleaner phrasing.
- Keep GitHub Pages only if it reflects meaningful use; otherwise replace with a stronger enterprise platform or remove.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is highly repetitive with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same core platforms.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid repeating it elsewhere without added context.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use in recent work and signal level/scope where possible.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop “HTML5” and “CSS3” unless versioning matters; simpler phrasing feels more current and senior.
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers: “front-end implementation,” “light scripting,” “serverless edge functions,” or “deployment automation” to show practical use, not just exposure.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie 1–2 tools to outcomes in recent roles instead of listing them here (e.g., GTM for analytics setup, Workers for search/performance, GitHub Actions for deployment workflow).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- Consider removing jQuery if it’s no longer a meaningful part of your recent work.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function to show judgment, not just familiarity: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Consider renaming to “Automation, Work Management & Collaboration Tools” for clarity and keyword strength.
- If space allows, add a light proficiency cue tied to recent work: “Used to build communications workflows, intake systems, and cross-team coordination processes.”
- Keep only the strongest/recently used platforms; if Trello/Basecamp are older or light-use, cut them.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating them too prominently in all three places.
- Slack/Teams are low-signal unless central to operations leadership; they can be removed if space is tight.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful tools to include, but this line is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the strategic email/engagement depth shown in recent NACo roles. Tighten naming and, if possible, signal level of use or business context.

Suggested edit:
- Rename for clarity and breadth: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Rewrite as: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope in brief: **Enterprise/member communications, newsletter operations, journey automation**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, list it first to reflect recency and strength.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Multi-channel communications operations” and multiple work-experience bullets on email/newsletters; keep this item tool-focused, not responsibility-focused.
- Avoid adding generic terms like “email strategy” here unless removing similar phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early platform/content ownership, and any concrete output or scale.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital media function…”
- Tighten scope and avoid generic phrasing like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows”; name outcomes instead: website refresh, livestream production, weekly video series, channel operations.
- Add measurable detail if available: number of livestreams/events supported, frequency/views of weekly videos, size of web/email/social operation, or team size.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital media team, supporting web, email, social and multimedia operations. Contributed to a major website refresh, produced livestreams and a recurring weekly video update, and helped formalize day-to-day digital workflows while mentoring a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- “Strengthening workflows” repeats later governance/operations themes; keep this entry more execution-focused.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generically and underplays the most distinctive achievement: launching NACo’s first podcast. Since later roles already cover broad digital/media leadership, this item should emphasize foundational innovation, research support, and first-of-its-kind multimedia work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to lead with the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities, while expanding digital storytelling capacity.”
- Make the podcast achievement more concrete: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Tighten vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” to something more active: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy-focused outreach.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, podcast episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content/multimedia” language already covered more strongly in later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here; later positions better establish management and operational ownership.
